rewrites.note: Built from the visitors' words, then masked. Brand searches bring 100% of the clicks, and 5 of the 17 brand queries add a category word to the name (8% of clicks). 6 of the 8 other queries name the job and the tools involved (query-1 (non-brand), query-2 (non-brand), query-3 (non-brand) are examples). There are no confirmed ads to borrow from. Our own headline and those words are masked, so each option shows which words fill each bracket.

headline.option: Small line above: [brand] + [the category word brand searchers add]. H1: [the job the non-brand queries name, as an outcome]
headline.why: Brand searchers (100% of clicks) need the name and category confirmed; the outcome in the H1 is for everyone else. The current H1 leads with the category.

headline.option: [The verb the non-brand queries use] + [the tools they name], and get [the result], without [the manual step]
headline.why: 6 of the 8 non-brand queries are phrased as a job with the tools named, not as a category.

subheadline.option: [Spell out the acronym once]. Works with [the tools named in the non-brand queries], so you can [the job, in their words].
subheadline.why: Removes the unexplained acronym and turns the mechanism into a benefit, in the visitors' terms.

subheadline.option: [Who it is for] use it to [two of the jobs the queries name], with [one proof point you have].
subheadline.why: Adds "who" and a first piece of proof to the hero.

primary_cta.option: [The verb the non-brand queries use] + [what they get first], e.g. "Connect your first account"
primary_cta.why: Says what happens after the click in the visitors' own verb; the current label names the sign-up type, not the result.

primary_cta.option: Keep the label, add a line under the button: [what happens next, how long it takes]
primary_cta.why: Lowers the commitment without changing the offer; the FAQ already states the setup time.

changes: Add a proof bar right under the hero CTAs.

Add a proof section (named quotes with results) before the FAQ.
Keep the FAQ: its 6 questions already cover coverage, how it works, several accounts, security, getting started and setup time.

tests.decision: Not enough traffic for an A/B test at any of these rates, and conversion is not measured yet. Ship the changes, then compare 4 weeks before with 4 weeks after on the proxies (engagement rate, share reaching pricing) and, once it exists, the CTA click event.
hypotheses: If the H1 leads with the visitor's outcome, then the share of sessions that reach pricing rises, because the current hero names only the category.
If proof sits under the hero CTA, then CTA clicks per session rise, because the page has no proof at all today.
If the primary CTA says what happens after the click, then CTA clicks rise, because the label names the sign-up type, not the result.
